pr_title: Handle zwave_js metadata/value updates when the unit changes
pr_body:
## Proposed change
In https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/62325 we are seeing a device change units on one of its values after startup. Because we get the unit of measurement during startup, HA currently doesn't detect this unit change properly. With this change, we do. In this particular case, two events get fired, a `metadata updated` event and `value updated` event, which in combination recalibrate the values on the device, but with this change should have no impact to the user.

~~We can reduce the code complexity once this gets merged and released: https://github.com/home-assistant-libs/zwave-js-server-python/pull/342~~

issue_context.title: Sensor temperature reading doesn't match Z-wave reported value
issue_context.body:
### The problem

A new Zooz ZSE40 700 series multi-sensor is reporting a temperature reading 90 degrees F higher than ambient temp.  After a hub reboot (no waking of the device, just a hub reboot) the reported temp came back into reality for a couple hours and then shot back up to about 90 degrees over.  The device's temp reading follows the ups and downs during the day but are always about 90 degrees higher than ambient temp.

This is where it gets even more interesting.  Looking at the Z-wave JS logs I can find the device's logging and the reported temp is accurate.  So while the z-wave communication suggests accurate readings, somewhere after that the temp reading gets ~90 degrees added to it.

Attached is an image of the history report for the device.
Attached is the z-wave JS log showing the accurate temp being sent.
Attached is the device page showing the bad reading.

![ZSE40_700_temp_history_graph](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/91510052/146682652-fd37e79d-75af-41dd-b0cb-aec8c9910b5d.png)
[ZSE40_700_zwave_log.txt](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/7741137/ZSE40_700_zwave_log.txt)
![ZSE40_700_device_page](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/91510052/146682672-1606b605-f585-43ab-bfde-1c02a606fc58.png)



### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2021.12.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Z-wave JS  (possibly)

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
2021-12-18T23:21:22.831Z SERIAL « 0x011000040025083105014a1ba03105bb008d                              (18 bytes)
2021-12-18T23:21:22.832Z CNTRLR   [Node 037] [Multilevel Sensor] Air temperature: metadata updated  [Endpoint 0]
2021-12-18T23:21:22.833Z CNTRLR   [Node 037] [~] [Multilevel Sensor] Air temperature: 70.14 => 70.7 [Endpoint 0]
2021-12-18T23:21:22.833Z SERIAL » [ACK]                                                                   (0x06)
2021-12-18T23:21:22.834Z DRIVER « [Node 037] [REQ] [ApplicationCommand]
                                  └─[MultilevelSensorCCReport]
                                      type:  Air temperature
                                      scale: Fahrenheit
                                      value: 70.72
```


### Additional information

This is the first 700 series z-wave device I have installed.  I have 2 dozen other z-wave devices working fine, including 4 other temp\humidity sensors.  All devices are z-wave plus.  The device in question is about 25 feet from the hub with no barriers other than a closet wall.

Hub hardware is an Intel NUC10i7, Samsung 970 EVO Plus SSD, 16 GB DDR4, Zooz Z-Wave Plus S2 USB stick.

All HA updates and integration updates have been applied.  Nothing in the HA logs looks out of the ordinary.

OK, this is interesting...

The z-wave traffic for the device is sending back Celsius readings.  See the attached log snippet.  You can see the transition from F to C with an accurate Celsius temp value being sent.

The issue is why HA isn't picking up that it's already in Fahrenheit when it's in Fahrenheit. Is that on our end, or theirs?

I think the unit of measurement of the entity is static after the entity has been created. If the unit in the driver changes during runtime, then HA does not recognize that, and so if the initial unit was fixed to C, any new F values would be incorrectly converted. The unit should either not be fixed, or HA should properly handle the `"metadata updated"` event, if the driver is properly sending that. Currently HA ignores that event if the value ID has already been discovered.

A restart of HA should also fix it if the units change.

A restart of HA did temporarily fix the problem back when I first discovered the issue.  But it only lasted for a couple hours before reverting back to a reading 90 degrees higher than the ambient temp..  Also, I can't remember for sure, but I think the original unit of measurement was F when the device was installed.

Update:
I reset the device's temp scale back to F yesterday.  Today I applied the HA 2021.12.4 update.  The device in HA has reverted back to the very high temp reading in the HA front end.  Restarting HA didn't resolve the problem.

I should say, the HA UI displays the sensor's reported 69 degrees at 90 degrees greater than reported by the device.

It will help to debug the issue (and prove whether my theory is correct or not!) if you turn on debug logging in HA. You can add this snippet to your `configuration.yaml` temporarily, restart HA after editing.

```yaml

  logs:
    homeassistant.components.zwave_js: debug
    zwave_js_server: debug
```

This will allow us to see the state of the node metadata when HA starts up, and whether it changes or not during runtime, and what temperature values the driver is reporting to HA. If you can produce the states of not working, and then working (or vice-versa), and upload the resulting log, that should hopefully confirm the problem.

After changing the device scale, you need to exclude and include it again (without resetting it). HA doesn't know that the scale has changed to reconfigure itself.

The HA configuration I posted above is to produce debug logs in HA, these logs go in the file `home-assistant.log`. The driver logs are still useful, but we really need to see what messages HA is getting about the air temperature. Without those logs we don't know what HA is doing (or not doing). 

When you restart HA the log file is overwritten, I think it might keep one old copy. So make sure you are manually saving the files prior to restart, if you do a restart.

Also, I'm not sure what the goal of changing the configuration setting is? The original issue submission did not mention anything about this. Adding another variable to the equation just makes it more complicated. Can you leave the setting at the unit you prefer, and then capture the problem?

I actually have another version of this device (Vision) in a test network, maybe I can try to reproduce it.

OK, I was able to reproduce this. It turns out changing the config parameter is the root of this issue, at least in my reproduction. The default temperature for this device is Celsius. The sensor was created with a C value and HA converted to my unit to F.

```
2022-01-05 22:36:03 DEBUG (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.zwave_js] Discovered entity: ZwaveDiscoveryInfo(node=Node(node_id=3), primary_value=Value(value_id='3-49-0-Air temperature'), assumed_state=False, platform='sensor', platform_data=NumericSensorDataTemplateData(entity_description_key='temperature', unit_of_measurement='°C'), additional_value_ids_to_watch=set(), platform_hint='numeric_sensor', platform_data_template=NumericSensorDataTemplate(static_data=None), entity_registry_enabled_default=True)
```

I switched the configuration parameter temp reporting unit from C to F. After a little bit of time, the next temperature report was indeed in F, and HA reported the value by converting the F value as if it were C. Z-Wave JS detects the unit change and sends a metadata updated message along with the new value. HA does not react to the metadata updated message, only the value change.

```
2022-01-05 22:48:25 DEBUG (MainThread) [zwave_js_server] Received message:
WSMessage(type=<WSMsgType.TEXT: 1>, data='{"type":"event","event":{"source":"node","event":"metadata updated","nodeId":3,"args":{"commandClassName":"Multilevel Sensor","commandClass":49,"endpoint":0,"property":"Air temperature","metadata":{"type":"number","readable":true,"writeable":false,"label":"Air temperature","ccSpecific":{"sensorType":1,"scale":1},"unit":"°F"},"propertyName":"Air temperature","nodeId":3}}}', extra='')

2022-01-05 22:48:25 DEBUG (MainThread) [zwave_js_server] Received message:
WSMessage(type=<WSMsgType.TEXT: 1>, data='{"type":"event","event":{"source":"node","event":"value updated","nodeId":3,"args":{"commandClassName":"Multilevel Sensor","commandClass":49,"endpoint":0,"property":"Air temperature","newValue":79.91,"prevValue":22.17,"propertyName":"Air temperature"}}}', extra='')

2022-01-05 22:48:25 DEBUG (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.zwave_js.entity] [sensor.4_in_1_sensor_air_temperature] Value Air temperature/None changed to: 79.91
```

The HA restart fixes it since the metadata is re-loaded when the integration is loaded. I can't comment on the observation that the sensor value will revert to a bad state later, however that would only occur if the device starts reporting the unit incorrectly. I'll leave my test system running to see if that happens.

So the platforms probably need to handle metadata updates to adjust their units. These events arrive at different times though, will updating the unit when the metadata updated is received cause the sensor value to spike temporarily, until the value update comes in? Does some internal conversion need to be performed to make the value and unit consistent until the value update is received?

Initial log with C to F changes: [home-assistant.log.1.log](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/7820057/home-assistant.log.1.log)
Restart: [home-assistant.log](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/7820055/home-assistant.log)
Driver: [zwavejs_current.log](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/7820037/zwavejs_current.log)

The change back and forth from F to C was Zooz's idea to gain some insight into the problem.  The device came with F set as the default (to the best of my recollection) and it sent accurate F temps (according to the zwave logs) from the start but the HA device page showed way high temps.  That prompted the wonder about if there was a F-to-C translation going on.

**Attached** are the HA logs as they look today.  They may not be what you want as I gather you wanted them exported at certain points.  I wish I knew that these were the logs you wanted because it was a lengthy process to gather the info above.  Still, they are recent enough you may find what you need.  I renamed the .1 file because I couldn't attach it otherwise.
[home-assistant.log](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/7823189/home-assistant.log)
[home-assistant.log.1.txt](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/7823195/home-assistant.log.1.txt)

All other zwave devices in my network handle config changes on the fly without having to exclude\re-include them.  It seems to be a serious handicap if it were the case that re-inclusion was necessary for a tweak.  Be that as it may.

> The device came with F set as the default and it sent accurate F temps (according to the zwave logs) from the start but the HA device page showed way high temps. That prompted the wonder about if there was a F-to-C translation going on.

Sounds like a device problem then. I bet even though it defaulted to F, it actually reported values in C at the beginning, and then changed later. I have the Vision version of this exact same device (Zooz rebrands the Vision, probably with some firmware tweaks), the ZP3111-5, and it defaults to C and the initial reports are in C. The only way to confirm this would be to exclude and factory reset the device, then re-include it, while capturing all those logs. (It might be enough to just exclude and re-include if the settings are reset upon exclusion.)

> I wish I knew that these were the logs you wanted because it was a lengthy process to gather the info above.

I did ask for HA debug logs, and provided an HA configuration setting. In the future I'll remember to be more specific.

> All other zwave devices in my network handle config changes on the fly without having to exclude\re-include them. It seems to be a serious handicap if it were the case that re-inclusion was necessary for a tweak. Be that as it may.

Excluding the device is not a viable option and isn't necessary, see my previous comment. Excluding the device resets the config parameters in some cases. For example, this ZP3111-5 reverts back to the default Celsius if you exclude and re-include.

**kpine and others**, thank you for all of your research into this.  I continue to be impressed by you guys.

If we are concluding that this is a device issue, does this info make its way back to Zooz?

Kpine, could you include a link to the Vision version of this device.  Thanks.

> If we are concluding that this is a device issue, does this info make its way back to Zooz?

That's not what _my_ conclusion is. I was saying that if a device is configured to report F, and it instead reports some values as C, it's not working as intended. Even if it is behaving this way, HA should still be able to handle the reported values correctly.

I don't think there's anything to take to Zooz unless you can prove a problem with the device, by capturing logs starting from inclusion and until the problem surfaces. If the device switches between reporting F and C values, and you have it configured for F, then you have a valid support case (which the vendor may decide to not even fix). Or maybe they will say that changing the config param does mean you need to exclude and include (could be different behavior than my model) and it will work properly.

> 
> Kpine, could you include a link to the Vision version of this device. Thanks.

http://www.visionsecurity.com.tw/index.php?option=product&lang=en&task=pageinfo&id=297&belongid=313&index=1
https://devices.zwave-js.io/?jumpTo=0x0109:0x2021:0x2101:0.0

Excluding the device shouldn't reset the parameters, as that's required for a device to change its capabilities. This is how the ZEN17 intentionally works when you change the sensor type. As we all know, anything is impossible though.

I have one of these Zooz sent me that I can throw on my test network later.

Ok, I learned something new, thanks. This is only standardized for Configuration CC V4 and later. So for earlier versions it probably depends on the device. yes, mine is a ZSE40 ver 2 700 series, firmware 32.32
